slides.title: Headers: free defence from the server
slides.summary: A handful of HTTP response headers turn on browser protections with no change to your app code.
body: Browsers ship many protections that are off by default for compatibility. Security headers switch them on for your site.
<mark>Set security headers once, at the CDN or server, so every response gets them, including error pages.</mark>

body.note: Check a deployed site with your browser's DevTools (Network → response headers) or a public scanner such as securityheaders.com.

cells.text: Unwanted use of camera, mic, etc.

viz.html: X-XSS-Protection is obsolete. Omit it or set it to 0.

slides.title: Content Security Policy (CSP)
slides.summary: CSP tells the browser which scripts, styles and connections are allowed, so injected code doesn't run.
body: A CSP is an allowlist for what the page may load and run. Its biggest job is to stop XSS payloads from executing even if they get into the HTML.
Domain allowlists (script-src cdn.example.com) are easy to bypass through JSONP endpoints and open redirects on those domains. A strict CSP uses nonces or hashes instead:

ul: the server generates a random nonce per response and puts it on each legitimate <script>;
'strict-dynamic' lets those trusted scripts load further scripts;
injected inline scripts and event handlers have no nonce, so they're blocked.

body: <mark>Start with Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only, collect violation reports, fix them, then enforce.</mark>

steps.caption: Deploy the policy in report-only mode first.

item.label: Fix violations
item.sub: Move inline handlers to code, add nonces

Switch to the enforcing header and keep reporting on.

slides.title: HSTS, nosniff, Referrer-Policy and COOP
slides.summary: The other headers each close one specific gap. Most are one line.

ul: Strict-Transport-Security makes the browser use HTTPS for your domain for max-age seconds, even if the user types http://.
X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff stops the browser guessing a file's type, so an uploaded “image” can't run as a script.
Referrer-Policy controls how much of the current URL is sent to other sites. URLs often contain IDs and tokens.
Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin cuts the link between your window and pages that open it or that it opens.

body.text: Adding Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp to COOP makes the page cross-origin isolated. That unlocks SharedArrayBuffer and precise timers, which are otherwise restricted because of Spectre-style attacks.
